question: Why did the rotated native trace contain two old-token HTTP 401 upgrades before one CreateHubToken request?

confirmed: The Hub observer recorded two /v1/listen upgrade-result responses with status 401 at 2026-09-06T03:33:18.396Z and 2026-09-06T03:33:18.406Z. Both carried the same old token SHA-256.
The issuer observer recorded exactly one successful Account_20151111.CreateHubToken request at 2026-09-06T03:33:18.482Z, returning the new token SHA-256.

The next /v1/listen upgrade returned 101 at 2026-09-06T03:33:18.492Z with the new token SHA-256. The later /v1/proactive 101 at 2026-09-06T03:33:43.779Z reused that new token and had no corresponding CreateHubToken request.

Pinned Poco 1.7.9 WebSocket::connect performs an initial handshake and, when it receives 401, drains that response, calls HTTPCredentials::authenticate, and sends one second handshake request before reporting a final 401. This source permits two HTTP upgrade attempts inside one native open call; its exact match to the loaded Moth library build is unproven.
Pinned ClientCloudConnection::authenticateAndOpen has one outer 401 branch: invalidateToken(), then one authenticateAndOpenOnce() call. Its source does not contain a second token-refresh branch.
conclusion.mechanism: The most source-consistent sequence is: cached Bearer token -> Poco handshake attempt 1 (401) -> Poco handshake attempt 2 (401) -> native ClientCloudConnection catches final 401 -> invalidateToken() -> one CreateHubToken fetch -> new-token handshake (101).
conclusion.confidence: Observed: two rejected requests with the same old token hash, one new CreateHubToken response and successful new-token upgrades. Source-consistent inference: both 401s belong to one Poco constructor; exact loaded build and attempt grouping remain unproven.

pocoSource.defaultCredentials: The three-argument WebSocket constructor uses static _defaultCreds. HTTPCredentials::authenticate changes Authorization only for Basic/Digest challenges. Same old-token hashes on both 401s are observed; attribution to one constructor remains inferred.

firmwarePin.reason: The firmware recipe pins the Poco 1.7.9 source tag, but the native library byte image is not in the local archive. The available sibling Pegasus libPocoNet.so.48 has SONAME libPocoNet.so.48 and a GCC 5.4.1 comment; the downloaded upstream 1.7.9 source reports libversion 49. Those facts are insufficient to equate the Moth SHA-256 library with an unmodified upstream build.

supported: The duplicate 401s are consistent with one Poco WebSocket constructor performing its built-in one-request 401 handshake retry, followed by the native wrapper's single retry after the second 401.
The issuer trace proves one, not two, native CreateHubToken fetches after rotation.
The two Notification_20150505.NewRobotToken issuer rows are separate calls and are not CreateHubToken retries.
inference: The two 401s likely belong to the same Poco constructor based on inspected source behavior; exact Moth library build and attempt grouping are unproven.
The observer does not establish WWW-Authenticate presence or native exception timing.
notClaimed: A byte-for-byte identification of the Moth libPocoNet.so.48 build
That the explicit SURPRISE trigger proves natural proactive opportunity detection

futureObserver.goal: Prove request grouping and distinguish Poco handshake retry from native token refetch without recording credentials.
perUpgrade: connectionAttemptId generated at the native open/authenticateAndOpen boundary
wwwAuthenticatePresent boolean and, if needed, a hash of the sanitized challenge scheme
Poco response reason and exception code only
perNativeAuth: CreateHubToken request/result count tied to connectionAttemptId and returned tokenSha256
futureObserver.privacy: Never record Authorization values, access keys, secret keys, JWT contents, response bodies, or certificates; retain hashes and status metadata only.
